source_text.body:
Archive Trello boards into a Google Doc with Claude Code
An HR leader used Claude Code to archive 10 Trello boards and 3,000 cards into a 1,000-page Google Doc in 19 minutes; the guide also cites cancelling subscriptions and recovering photos.
Done with
CC
Claude Code
What they did
The guide gives this only one sentence. An HR leader archived 10 Trello boards and 3,000 cards into a single 1,000-page Google Doc. The guide doesn't describe the setup, the prompts, or where the person stepped in. It links to an HR-focused Substack post for the original account.
How it went
The archive took 19 minutes and produced a 1,000-page Google Doc. The guide gives no detail on accuracy, errors, or any checking afterward.
Worth knowing
The guide says Claude Code needs a paid plan (Pro is $20 a month). It also advises working in a dedicated folder, keeping backups, and telling the agent never to delete anything.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
I have a Trello workspace with [number] boards I want to archive. Using my exported Trello JSON files in [folder path], pull every card with its title, description, comments, checklists, and attachments links, and compile them into one organized document grouped by board and list, saved as [Word or Markdown file] that I can upload to Google Docs. You're done when every board and card is included and you've given me a count of boards and cards processed. Show me your plan before you delete or overwrite any files.
Original source: https://ccforeveryone.com/guides/claude-code-for-non-developers
